chat_server_config:
# vllm serve --config for Gemma 4 26B-A4B QAT on the Radeon VII. Benchmarks: README.md
# Built with repack_gemma4_qat.py: all linear weights bit-exact from Google's QAT Q4_0 GGUF (int4, group size 32),
# embedding and lm_head int4 (round-to-nearest, group size 32).
model: /models/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-q4_0-ct
served-model-name: google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-qat
# gfx906 has no native bf16.
dtype: float16
# Do not load the vision tower (1.1 GiB in fp16), which would leave no room for the KV cache.
language-model-only: true
# The maximum with the KV cache below. Peak 16263 MiB of 16368 in the stress test (a 33300-token prompt).
max-model-len: 34816
# Set explicitly instead of gpu-memory-utilization, whose profiling leaves ~0.8 GiB unused on this GPU.
kv-cache-memory-bytes: 950000000
# vLLM uses Triton attention for Gemma 4 (head sizes 256 and 512), which supports quantized KV caches.
# int8 with a scale per token and head is the format closest to llama.cpp's q8_0. fp16 would halve the context.
kv-cache-dtype: int8_per_token_head
# One request at a time, like parallel = 1 of the llama.cpp preset: every additional sequence needs its own
# sliding-window KV cache (~0.2 GiB).
max-num-seqs: 1
# The prefill chunk. Larger chunks need more activation memory.
max-num-batched-tokens: 512
# CUDA graphs only for single-token decoding: capturing the default 51 sizes takes several GiB.
compilation-config: {"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1]}
enable-prefix-caching: true
# Prefix cache blocks evicted from the GPU are kept in 8 GiB of pinned RAM, so that a returning conversation needs
# no new prompt processing (a 15000-token prompt: 0.2 s instead of 27 s). Needs VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0.
kv-offloading-size: 8
kv-offloading-backend: native
reasoning-parser: gemma4
enable-auto-tool-choice: true
tool-call-parser: gemma4
# Sampling: generation_config.json of the model (temperature 1.0, top-k 64, top-p 0.95), as recommended by Google.

# group size 32), the embedding and the lm_head int8 (round-to-nearest, group size 128). 15.4 GiB on the GPU with the

# vLLM uses Triton attention for Gemma 4 (head sizes 256 and 512), which supports quantized KV caches.

    resources:
      reservations:
        devices:
          - driver: nvidia
            capabilities: [gpu]
            count: all

services:
  vllm-flash-next:
    <<: *gpu
    # The single-RTX-3090 runtime of https://github.com/DominikBucko/qwen38-flash-next-3090 (a vLLM build with
    # CPU expert kernels for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) with image and video input, the vision tower on the CPU: the image of
    # this directory, built by ../.github/workflows/deploy-docker-vllm-rtx3090-flash-next.yml. See README.md.
    image: ghcr.io/agenttix/agx-ai/vllm-flash-next:latest
    container_name: vllm-flash-next
    # The runtime takes the API key from VLLM_API_KEY.
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - >-
        VLLM_API_KEY="$$LLAMA_API_KEY" exec /usr/local/bin/qwen38-serve
        /root/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--albucino--Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-FP8PLE/snapshots/ef554143369a706525336f6b42a09094835dc077
    env_file:

    # docs/tuning.md). Benchmarks on agx-z2e: ../vllm-agx-z2e/README.md#qwen38-flash-next
    environment:
      SERVED_MODEL_NAME: Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
      PORT: "8000"
      # The full trained context of 262144 tokens (the runtime's default: 135168), like llama.cpp. It fits because the
      # token embedding is in pinned RAM (QWEN38_EMBED_UVA, -1.18 GiB, looked up over PCIe) and fewer experts stay on
      # the GPU (see ../vllm-agx-z2e/README.md). The KV cache holds 287594 tokens; the runtime needs ~1.05 times the context. Peak

      MAX_MODEL_LEN: "262144"
      KV_CACHE_MEMORY_BYTES: "5150000000"
      QWEN38_EMBED_UVA: "1"

      QWEN38_GPU_SHARE_FRAC: "0.3"

label: z2e vLLM Qwen3.8-27B pth-flash-attn, FP16 state, MTP 3
chat_server_config:
# vllm serve --config for Qwen3.8-27B on the RTX 3090 of agx-z2e. Benchmarks: README.md
# GPTQ int4 (group size 128) with int4 embedding and lm_head, 13.1 GiB on the GPU without the vision tower. The
# quantized embedding needs ../vllm/vllm.patch. The mtp-int8 revision has the MTP head in int8 (0.4 GiB).
model: JRamirez-UAB/Qwen3.8-27B-GPTQ-W4A16-embed-int4-24GB
revision: mtp-int8
served-model-name: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B
# Do not load the vision tower (0.9 GiB), which would cost ~25k tokens of context.
language-model-only: true
# The maximum with the KV cache below (168848 tokens, 1.07 times the context: the scheduler needs some extra blocks
# for the recurrent states). Peak 21036 MiB with a 153000-token prompt.
max-model-len: 155648
# Set explicitly instead of gpu-memory-utilization, whose profiling leaves less for the KV cache. vLLM still checks at
# startup that gpu-memory-utilization of the GPU memory is free, so it is set below what the desktop leaves free.
kv-cache-memory-bytes: 6400000000
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.8
# int8 with a scale per token and head (the format closest to llama.cpp's q8_0) fits twice the context of BF16. It is
# read by the pth-flash-attn kernel of ../vllm (CUSTOM, from HyperQwen, see ../vllm-rtx3090-hyperqwen/README.md),
# which is faster at long contexts than the Triton attention with the split-KV fix of ../vllm/vllm.patch (100k tokens
# of context: 66-69 instead of 41 t/s). FlashAttention 2 supports no quantized KV cache, and the FP8 cache of
# FlashInfer allows no full CUDA graphs with MTP (chat 51 instead of 81 t/s).
kv-cache-dtype: int8_per_token_head
attention-backend: CUSTOM
# The recurrent state of the 48 Gated DeltaNet layers in FP16 instead of FP32 (as in HyperQwen): 6.5 % more tokens in
# the KV cache.
mamba-ssm-cache-dtype: float16
# The prefill chunk. 4096 was not faster.
max-num-batched-tokens: 2048
# Full CUDA graphs for decoding, for up to 4 sequences with 3 tokens each (MTP).
compilation-config: {"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 16]}
# Every sequence needs its own recurrent state for the 48 Gated DeltaNet layers.
max-num-seqs: 4
# MTP with the model's own MTP head: 2 drafted tokens. 3 were not clearly faster and leave less context.
# The drafter takes its attention backend from here.
speculative-config: {"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "attention_backend": "CUSTOM"}
enable-prefix-caching: true
# Prefix cache blocks evicted from the GPU are kept in 16 GiB of pinned RAM, so that a returning conversation needs
# no new prompt processing (a 25k-token prompt: 4.0 s instead of 25.8 s). It takes no GPU memory.
kv-offloading-size: 16
kv-offloading-backend: native
reasoning-parser: qwen3
enable-auto-tool-choice: true
tool-call-parser: qwen3_coder
# Sampling: generation_config.json of the model (temperature 1.0, top-k 20, top-p 0.95), as recommended by Qwen.

chat_server_config:
# HyperQwen (https://github.com/syv-ai/HyperQwen): Qwen3.8-27B on the RTX 3090 of agx-z2e, tuned for agentic coding
# with one user and one or a few agents. See README.md for the settings and the measurements behind them.
# The same port as ../vllm-rtx3090 and ../llama-cpp-rtx3090 (9931): only one of them fits on the GPU at a time.
#
#   docker compose run --rm prepare   # once: download and requantize the model into ~/.cache/vllm-models/hyperqwen
#   docker compose up -d
#
# The API key is the one of the llama.cpp servers (LLAMA_API_KEY in ../llama-cpp/llama-cpp.env), so that
# clients work with all of them.

x-hyperqwen: &hyperqwen
  # HyperQwen's image of its commit ce9615c (2026-10-22, vLLM 0.31.0; published as ghcr.io/syv-ai/qwen38-27b-rtx3090
  # before the project was renamed) with the vision tower on the CPU: the image of this directory, built by
  # ../.github/workflows/deploy-docker-vllm-rtx3090-hyperqwen.yml. See README.md.
  image: ghcr.io/agenttix/agx-ai/vllm-hyperqwen:latest
  volumes:
    - /home/mika/.cache/vllm-models/hyperqwen:/app/models
    - cache:/cache

services:
  prepare:
    <<: *hyperqwen
    profiles: [prepare]
    command: prepare

  vllm:
    <<: *hyperqwen
    container_name: vllm-rtx3090-hyperqwen
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              capabilities: [gpu]
              count: all
    # The CPU KV cache (KV_OFFLOAD_GB) is a file in /dev/shm. The container has its own /dev/shm instead of the host's
    # (ipc: host), as the launcher deletes the offload files of /dev/shm that no process of its container maps,
    # which would include those of other vLLM containers.
    shm_size: 36gb
    env_file:
      - ../llama-cpp/llama-cpp.env
    environment:
      # The torch.compile, Triton and FlashInfer caches are in $HOME (the cache volume).
      HOME: /cache
      PORT: "8000"
      # The model was prepared with `docker compose run --rm prepare`.
